title: Sunscreen Stick Coverage

caption:
One quick swipe of a sunscreen stick gives less than 20% of its labeled SPF protection.

Here's what actually happens when you apply a sunscreen stick:

1. Single Swipe — A quick pass deposits a patchy wax layer full of microscopic gaps.
2. Thin UV Film — Without built-up thickness, UV rays pass directly through low-density areas.
3. 20 Percent SPF — Lab tests measure SPF at 2mg per square cm, requiring 4 full passes to reach rated barrier power.

When choosing sun protection, application density matters far more than brand claims.

No magic shortcut — real protection requires sufficient film thickness.
